title: Which option?
description: Pick the option that makes the command do exactly what the task says.

cards.prompt: Mira wants `ls` to show hidden files (names that start with a dot) as well.
cards.why: `-a` means all: it includes the names that start with a dot. `-l` is the long format and `-R` goes into subdirectories.

cards.prompt: Mira wants `ls` to list the contents of every subdirectory too.
cards.why: `-R` is recursive: `ls` descends into every directory below.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants a long listing with file sizes shown as `4.0K` or `1.2M` instead of bytes.
cards.why: `-l` gives the long format and `-h` makes the sizes human-readable. `-a` would only add hidden files.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to copy the whole directory `art` with everything in it to `backup`.
cards.why: `-r` makes `cp` recursive, which a directory needs. Without it, `cp` refuses to copy a directory.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to create `a/b/c` in one go, even if `a` and `b` do not exist yet.
cards.why: `mkdir -p` creates every missing parent directory. Without `-p`, `mkdir` fails when `a/b` does not exist.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to see what is inside `release.tar.gz` without unpacking it.
cards.why: `-t` lists the contents. `-x` extracts, and `-c` creates a new archive, which would overwrite the file.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to create a bzip2-compressed archive `art.tar.bz2` from `art/`.
cards.why: `-j` selects bzip2. `-z` is gzip, `-J` is xz, and `-x` extracts instead of creating.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to find lines in `build.log` that contain `error`, whether it is written `error`, `Error` or `ERROR`.
cards.why: `-i` ignores case. `-v` inverts the match, `-c` only counts the lines and `-n` adds line numbers.

cards.prompt: Mira wants every line of `build.log` that does not contain `WARNING`.
cards.why: `-v` inverts the match and prints the lines that do not contain the pattern.

cards.prompt: Ada wants only the number of lines of `build.log` that contain `ERROR`.
cards.why: `-c` prints the count of matching lines instead of the lines.

cards.prompt: Ada wants every matching line of `build.log` with its line number in front.
cards.why: `-n` puts the line number before each match.

cards.prompt: Mira has a file of scores, one number per line, and wants them ordered by value, so that 9 comes before 10.
cards.why: `-n` sorts numerically. A plain `sort` compares text, so `10` would come before `9`.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants to count how often each line occurs in a sorted file, with the count in front.
cards.why: `uniq -c` prefixes each distinct line with its number of repeats. It only compares neighbouring lines, so the input should be sorted.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to watch new lines arrive at the end of a log file while the build is running.
cards.why: `-f` (follow) keeps `tail` running and prints new lines as they are appended.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to send exactly three ping requests to `198.51.100.7` and then stop.
cards.why: On Linux `-c` sets the count. A plain `ping` keeps sending until you press Ctrl+C.
